rationale.conceptual: The method involves nuanced choices of basis sets, gauge origins (London orbitals for HF/B3LYP, center-of-mass origin for CC2/CCSD), and the meaning of optical rotation tensors from linear response. Correctly implementing these distinct levels of theory across a set of molecules requires genuine understanding of correlated quantum chemistry methods, not a simple library call.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of geometry optimization for 13 molecules followed by 52 high-level single-point calculations (four methods per molecule), some of which (CCSD/aug-cc-pVDZ linear response) are computationally expensive. Coordinating the runs, parsing molecular structures from names, and assembling the outputs into the required CSV demands a robust, multi-stage orchestration script with careful environment setup.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running advanced quantum chemistry calculations (geometry optimizations and coupled-cluster linear-response optical rotation) for 13 molecules using four methods with specific basis sets and gauge-origin choices. This is a non-trivial computational chemistry pipeline needing deep domain expertise and careful orchestration of expensive CPU-bound calculations.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All calculations are CPU-bound (no GPU acceleration relevant for CCSD linear response). The aug-cc-pVDZ basis on molecules up to norbornenone requires moderate RAM (~16 GB peak) but the real cost is CPU hours, not memory or data volume.
